working_title: England's Atlantic Links: A Practical Guide to Golf in Devon and Cornwall for UK Visitors
angle: Devon and Cornwall are routinely overlooked as a golf destination in favour of Scotland, Ireland, and the English coasts that host the Open rota, yet the stretch of Atlantic coastline from North Devon through to the tip of Cornwall contains a remarkable concentration of genuine links golf. This post makes the practical case for a dedicated trip, covers the key courses to anchor an itinerary around, and flags a few things that catch first-timers out.
research_notes:
- The South West is England's second-strongest golfing region by ranked courses, with no fewer than fifteen courses inside England's Top 100 (top100golfcourses.com).
- Six courses have formally joined together as the 'Atlantic Links Golf Coast': Trevose, St Enodoc, Royal North Devon, Burnham & Berrow, and Saunton East and West (globalgolfermag.com).
- St Enodoc (Church Course), designed by James Braid in 1907, is described as 'the finest links in England outside the Open Championship rota' and ranks consistently in the world Top 100 (top100golfcourses.com / golfsouthwest.co.uk).
- Saunton East Course: designed by Herbert Fowler in the 1920s, set among the Braunton Burrows dune system. The East course features 14 par 4s; the exposed 136-yard 13th is a standout par 3. Sergio Garcia won the Boys' Amateur here in 1997 (bunkered.co.uk). Widely discussed as a potential future Open venue.
- Royal North Devon (Westward Ho!): founded 1864, described as the oldest golf course in England still playing over its original fairways (experiencebritain.co.uk). Often called 'ground zero for links golf in England'.
- Burnham & Berrow (Championship): Somerset links on the Bristol Channel coast, regularly used for Open Championship qualification (top100golfcourses.com).
- Trevose (Championship): designed by Harry Colt in 1925, sheltered by Trevose Head and six sandy bays. Conditions can vary dramatically depending on wind (globalgolfermag.com).
- Perranporth: described as 'probably the most underrated links course in the South West of England' with a Harry Colt design over 12 holes along the headland (top100golfcourses.com / golfsouthwest.co.uk).
- Geography note: North Devon courses (Saunton x2, Royal North Devon) cluster together near Barnstaple/Braunton; Cornwall courses (St Enodoc, Trevose, Perranporth) cluster further south-west. Sensible itinerary splits into a North Devon base and a North Cornwall base (Rock/Wadebridge area for St Enodoc and Trevose).
- St Enodoc is located across the Camel Estuary from Trevose, near Rock/Wadebridge (globalgolfermag.com).
- Practical note: links courses in the region drain well and are playable year-round due to sand-based fairways (golfsouthwest.co.uk).
- Self-drive is the standard approach; public transport to these coastal venues is limited.
